aggressive_definition: High-grade incident prostate cancer, defined as Gleason score 8–10
aggressive_definition_excerpt: However, we did not find any significant association between tea intake and low- (Gleason <7) or high-grade (Gleason 8-10) prostate cancer incidence.
cohort_total_n_excerpt: We conducted a prospective cohort study of 6,016 men who were enrolled in the Collaborative Cohort Study between 1970 and 1973 and followed up to December 31, 2007.
reason: The prospective cohort analyzed both overall prostate cancer incidence and grade-specific incidence, including high-grade prostate cancer defined as Gleason 8–10.

estimate_classifications.endpoint_excerpt: The association was greatest among men who drank ≥ 7 cups of tea per day (HR: 1.50, 95% CI: 1.06 to 2.12), compared with the baseline of 0-3 cups/day.
